mainTopic: How the סוטה scroll must be written: material, ink, time of day, order, timing after the oath, and proper scroll form
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's rules for writing the מגילת סוטה and then adds the גמרא's own rules. The משנה says the scroll must be written on proper parchment, not on דיפתרא, because the פסוק says 'בספר'. It must also be written in erasable ink (דיו), not with קומוס or קנקנתום, because the פסוק says 'ומחה', so the writing has to wash off into the water. In the גמרא, רבא rules that a scroll written at night is פסולה. He learns this through a גזירה שוה on the word 'תורה', which links סוטה to משפט, and judgment is done only by day. A scroll written למפרע (out of order) is also פסולה, because 'these curses' must be written as they appear in the תורה. It is פסולה if it was written before the woman accepted the שבועה, since the פסוק mentions the oath before the writing. Finally, a scroll written like an informal letter (איגרת) is פסולה, because the תורה requires it to be written 'בספר'.

steps.title: The scroll must be proper parchment, not partly processed hide
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of unfit writing materials. דיפתרא is not allowed; only a real parchment scroll (מגילה) works, because the פסוק says 'בספר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He may not write it on] דיפתרא, only on a parchment scroll, as it says: 'in a scroll.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle of a sentence listing materials the כהן may NOT write the סוטה scroll on. Here it finishes with דיפתרא and says only a proper scroll is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'בספר' (in a scroll) in במדבר 5:23. A scroll means properly prepared parchment, so a half-finished hide like דיפתרא does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A hide that was only partly processed (salted and floured, but not treated with gallnuts)
A scroll of properly prepared parchment
As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)
'In a scroll' — the key word from the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence starts before this section. The opening words, which you can't see here, list other materials that are also not allowed, so 'דיפתרא' is the last item on a 'not on this' list.

phrases.english: [nor on] diftera (partly processed hide),
rather, only on a parchment scroll,
as it is said: 'in a scroll.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list of unfit writing materials, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגילת סוטה must be written on a proper parchment scroll, not on דיפתרא.

steps.title: The scroll must be written in ink that can be erased
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the scroll may not be written with קומוס, קנקנתום, or anything that leaves a lasting mark. It must be written with דיו, because the פסוק says 'ומחה', meaning the writing must be able to wash off.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not write with gum or with iron sulfate, or with anything that leaves a mark, only with ink, as it says: 'and he shall blot out.' That means writing that can be erased.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from the writing surface to the ink. Only erasable ink is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll's whole purpose is to be blotted out into the water the סוטה drinks. So the פסוק 'ומחה' teaches that the writing must be able to come off fully. Substances that leave a permanent mark cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Gum (a sticky tree resin)
Iron sulfate (vitriol), which leaves a lasting mark
Leaves a mark that stays
Ink (made from soot) that can be washed off
'And he shall blot out' — from the פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern: the details of how the scroll is made come straight from what the scroll has to do. It must be erased, so the ink must be erasable.

phrases.english: And he may not write with gum,
and not with iron sulfate,
and not with anything that leaves a lasting mark,
but only with ink,
as it is said: 'and he shall blot out,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:23, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: meaning writing that is able to be erased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the writing surface (step 1) to the writing ink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scroll must be written only in erasable ink (דיו), because it has to be blotted out.

steps.title: רבא: a scroll written at night is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא's ruling that a מגילת סוטה written at night is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said: A סוטה scroll that was written at night is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by adding a rule the משנה did not mention. According to רבא, the scroll must be written during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covered the material and the ink. רבא adds a rule about the time of writing. If the scroll was written at night, it cannot be used. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and expands the משנה
The scroll with the סוטה curses, which gets blotted into the water
At night
Unfit, invalid

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava says:
A sota scroll that one wrote at night is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְגִילַּת סוֹטָה שֶׁכְּתָבָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה — פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new rule about writing the scroll, on top of the משנה's rules about material and ink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילת סוטה written at night is פסולה.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבא's rule against writing at night.
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next move. The גמרא wants to know where רבא learns that the scroll must be written by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the סוטה פסוקים openly says 'by day'. So the גמרא asks for the source, and the answer will need a link to a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asks for the source or logic)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבא's ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that the scroll must be written by day.

steps.title: A word-link between סוטה and judgment proves it must be by day
steps.stepSummary: The source is a גזירה שוה on the word 'תורה'. It appears in the סוטה פסוק and in a פסוק about משפט (judgment). Judgment is done only by day, so the סוטה scroll must also be written by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'law' and 'law.' Here it is written: 'And the כהן shall do to her all this law.' And there it is written: 'According to the law which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment.' Just as judgment is by day, so too the סוטה scroll is by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by linking two פסוקים that share the word 'תורה'. This lets the rule from one place apply to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה section calls the process 'all this תורה' (במדבר 5:30). The פסוק in דברים 17:11 puts 'תורה' right next to 'משפט', and court judgment happens only in the daytime. Because the same word appears in both places, the daytime rule of משפט carries over to the סוטה scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from — introduces a גזירה שוה
A link between two פסוקים that share the same word, so a rule passes from one to the other
It is written here… and it is written there — compares the two פסוקים
Judgment, a court case
Just as… so too — carries the rule across

steps.whatToRemember: A מגילת סוטה written at night is פסולה. We learn this through a גזירה שוה ('תורה'–'תורה') from משפט, which is done only by day.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'תורה' here does not mean the whole Five Books. It means 'law' or 'procedure', the set of instructions for the סוטה.

phrases.english: It is learned from 'law' and 'law.'
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two different פסוקים, and that shared word is what links them.

phrases.english: It is written here (about sota):

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעָשָׂה לָהּ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת״,
phrases.english: 'And the priest shall do to her all this law,'
and it is written there (about judgment):

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ וְעַל הַמִּשְׁפָּט״,
phrases.english: 'According to the law which they shall teach you, and according to the judgment,'
just as judgment is by day,
so too the sota scroll is by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'תורה' links the סוטה scroll to משפט, which is done only by day.

steps.title: A scroll written out of order is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another rule: if the scroll was written למפרע (out of sequence), it is פסולה. The פסוק says 'these curses', meaning they must be written exactly as they appear in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote it out of order, it is unfit, as it is written: 'And he shall write these curses' — just as they are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues listing rules for writing the scroll. Now it says the words must be written in their correct order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'these curses', pointing to the specific curses in their place in the תורה. So the scroll has to copy them in the same order. Writing the later words before the earlier ones makes the scroll invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of order, not in the proper sequence
'These curses' — the curses of the סוטה
Just as it is written (in the תורה)
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: So far the מגילת סוטה needs proper parchment and erasable ink (from the משנה), and must be written by day and in the correct order (from the גמרא). The next steps add more rules.

phrases.english: If one wrote it out of order, it is unfit,
as it is written: 'And he shall write these curses,'
just as they are written.
phrases.notes: He means just as the curses are written in the תורה, in the same order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule about writing the scroll, after the night-time rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילת סוטה written out of order is פסולה, because the curses must be written as they appear in the תורה.

steps.title: The scroll must be written after the oath
steps.stepSummary: If the scroll is written before the סוטה accepts the שבועה, it is פסולה, because the פסוק mentions the oath first and the writing afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote the scroll before she accepted the oath, it is invalid. The פסוק first says 'and he shall make her swear,' and only afterward 'and he shall write.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another rule to its list: the order of the ceremony matters. The oath has to come first, and only then may the scroll be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the order of the פסוקים in פרשת סוטה. 'וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ' (פסוק 21) comes before 'וְכָתַב' (פסוק 23), so the תורה is setting a required order. This fits with the earlier rule about writing למפרע: here too, the תורה's sequence must be followed exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Oath; here, the oath the כהן has the סוטה accept
Before
'And he shall make her swear', the פסוק about the oath
'And he shall write', the פסוק about writing the scroll

phrases.english: If he wrote it before she accepted the oath upon herself,
it is invalid, as it says: 'And he shall make her swear,'
and afterward: 'And he shall write.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:23. Two פסוקים later, so the writing clearly comes after the oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another disqualification to the list that began with writing at night and writing למפרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילת סוטה written before the woman accepts the שבועה is פסולה, because the פסוקים put the oath before the writing.

steps.title: The scroll must be written like a proper scroll, not a letter
steps.stepSummary: If the scroll is written in the style of a letter (איגרת), it is פסולה, because the תורה says 'in a scroll'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote it like a letter, it is invalid. The תורה said 'in a scroll.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more disqualification: the scroll may not be written casually like an everyday letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בַּסֵּפֶר' tells us the writing must have the form of a real ספר, like a ספר תורה. A letter is written informally, so it does not count as a 'ספר', and the scroll is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A letter, an informal piece of writing
'In a scroll', the word in the פסוק that requires a proper scroll
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ used when quoting the תורה
Scoring lines on the parchment before writing, as done for a ספר תורה

steps.whatToRemember: So far the מגילת סוטה is פסולה if it is written at night, written out of order, written before the oath, or written like a letter. Each rule is learned from the wording or order of the פסוקים.

phrases.english: If he wrote it as a letter, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: Like a letter: written casually, without lines scored into the parchment the way a ספר תורה has them.

phrases.english: 'In a scroll,' the Merciful One said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of disqualifications with a rule about the form of the writing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילת סוטה written like a letter is פסולה, because the תורה requires it to be written 'בַּסֵּפֶר'.
